scope: Main terminal.run Gateway RPC admission, including approved commands; synthetic Gateway RPCs, not real OS-process limits.

leaseAndTerminalCases.test: workspace exec lease preserves FIFO, capacity and queuedMs for 200 queued requests
workspace exec lease removes timed-out work and admits the next waiter after release
workspace exec lease releases a slot after synchronous throws and asynchronous rejections
workspace exec lease does not let a stale double release over-admit while another lease is held
workspace exec lease grants up to capacity 2 immediately and queues the third
workspace exec lease does not block a different workspace key
workspace exec lease rejects with a typed timeout error when the slot never frees
terminal api workspace exec lease bounds concurrent terminal executions per workspace at capacity 2
terminal api workspace exec lease lets different workspaces run in parallel
terminal api workspace exec lease shares capacity across Windows case and slash variants and API instances
terminal api workspace exec lease keeps RPC method fallback inside the lease and releases after a Gateway failure
terminal api workspace exec lease queues approved work too and records admission timeout without executing it later
terminal api workspace exec lease reports a stable blocked result when the lease cannot be acquired in time
terminal api OpenClaw exec integration delegates allowed terminal commands to OpenClaw/Gateway instead of spawning a local shell
terminal api OpenClaw exec integration tries compatible OpenClaw exec RPC names and never falls back to PowerShell
terminal api OpenClaw exec integration returns an explicit unavailable result when OpenClaw exposes no direct terminal RPC
terminal api OpenClaw exec integration requires approval for dangerous commands before delegating to OpenClaw
terminal api OpenClaw exec integration records a bounded diagnostic for failed approved terminal commands
terminal api OpenClaw exec integration maps safe Gateway failure metadata to { success: false, code: 'ENOENT', exitCode: 1 }
terminal api OpenClaw exec integration maps safe Gateway failure metadata to { success: false, code: 'EACCES', exitCode: 1 }
terminal api OpenClaw exec integration maps safe Gateway failure metadata to { success: false, timedOut: true, exitCode: null }
terminal api OpenClaw exec integration maps safe Gateway failure metadata to { success: false, cancelled: true, exitCode: null }
terminal api OpenClaw exec integration does not record successful approved terminal commands
terminal api OpenClaw exec integration blocks mutating commands in read-only mode before reaching Gateway

rawEvidence.recovery: Keep the named private local archive; commands in gates reproduce the checks with $root set to an output directory.

priorRuns: Dirty-worktree red and green runs are development evidence only.
The final/ run used PATH Node v24.15.0; superseded by final-supported/ using existing Node v24.19.0 without changing system installation.
The first archived-spec validation failed on missing touchedAreas coverage; repaired before the clean candidate run.
Retention initially rejected not-yet-tracked evidence files; passed after staging and freezing the candidate.
limitations: Not full harness:ci, root unit suite, Electron E2E, packaged release, non-Windows or live-provider acceptance.
The 200-request burst uses fake timers and a real in-process lease manager; it is not a real Gateway throughput or latency benchmark.
Bounds concurrent RPC sequences only in one Main process. Releasing after RPC failure does not prove remote OS processes have stopped.
No terminal.open, runtime agent-exec, cross-process or search/writer/subtree/file-mutation budget claim.
No new scheduler, local-shell fallback, product-lock or frozen-default changes.
